outcome.answer:
To make item IDs change and update automatically during training in a generative search/recommendation system, the papers support using Semantic IDs (SIDs) but carefully managing their drift so already-learned retrieval/generation paths are not disrupted. One approach is to freeze the SID mappings for existing items while inserting new items, and warm-start the model so updates remain compatible; this “insert new-items, freeze old-items; warm-start when possible” principle helps prevent retrieval degradation from remapping-induced “SID semantic drift.” [1]

For user-pattern–aware updates, you can refresh interaction-informed SIDs and then align the refreshed SIDs back to the existing SID vocabulary so the retriever checkpoint stays compatible for warm-start fine-tuning, avoiding full rebuild-and-retrain. [2] Alternatively, for collaborative tokenizers, drift-aware continual tokenization can identify item-level drift confidence and reassign codes using a relaxed-to-strict strategy to limit unnecessary token changes. [5]

These differ in what they update: [1] focuses on topology preservation under dynamic item arrivals, [2] focuses on aligning refreshed collaborative semantics to prevent staleness, and [5] focuses on continual tokenizer updates guided by drift identification and constrained reassignment.
